description: Per standings row, use the stored season-to-date win count.

a.request: For each circuit country, take the driver standings at each race held there and average the drivers' season-to-date win counts (`driverStandings.wins` as stored) within each race, then average those per-race figures across the country's races so each race counts equally (ignoring missing values). Treat the simple mean of these country figures (each country counted once) as the overall benchmark and keep the countries strictly above it. Then take the mean figure of those kept countries and keep only the ones strictly above that second mean. For each remaining country, return the country, its average, how far it is above the overall benchmark, and how far it is above the second mean, without rounding.
a.sql: WITH race_avg AS (SELECT r.raceId, c.country, AVG(ds.wins) AS race_wins FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId WHERE ds.wins IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country), country_avg AS (SELECT country, AVG(race_wins) AS avg_wins FROM race_avg GROUP BY country), bench AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS b FROM country_avg), kept AS (SELECT country, avg_wins FROM country_avg, bench WHERE avg_wins > bench.b), second AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS m FROM kept) SELECT k.country, k.avg_wins AS average, k.avg_wins - bench.b AS above_benchmark, k.avg_wins - second.m AS above_second_mean FROM kept k, bench, second WHERE k.avg_wins > second.m

b.request: For each circuit country, take each race held there and average the stored season-to-date win counts (driverStandings.wins) across all driver standings rows for that race, then average those per-race figures across the country's races; keep countries whose average exceeds the mean of all countries' averages, then among those keep countries whose average exceeds the mean of that above-average group, and report each country's average wins, its difference from the overall country average, and its difference from the above-average group's average
b.sql: WITH race_avg AS (SELECT r.raceId, c.country, AVG(ds.wins) AS race_wins FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ds.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country), country_avg AS (SELECT country, AVG(race_wins) AS avg_wins FROM race_avg GROUP BY country), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS overall_avg FROM country_avg), above AS (SELECT ca.country, ca.avg_wins FROM country_avg ca, overall o WHERE ca.avg_wins > o.overall_avg), above_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS grp_avg FROM above) SELECT a.country, a.avg_wins AS average_wins, a.avg_wins - o.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall_avg, a.avg_wins - g.grp_avg AS diff_from_above_avg_group FROM above a, overall o, above_mean g WHERE a.avg_wins > g.grp_avg ORDER BY a.avg_wins DESC

c.request: For each circuit country, average the drivers' wins in the standings at each race held there, then average those race figures across the country's races. Which countries are above the average across countries? Among those, which are also above the average of that above-average group? For each, give the country, its average wins, how far it is above the overall average, and how far it is above the group average. Per standings row, use the stored season-to-date win count.
c.sql: WITH race_avg AS (SELECT r.raceId, c.country, AVG(ds.wins) AS race_wins FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country), country_avg AS (SELECT country, AVG(race_wins) AS avg_wins FROM race_avg GROUP BY country), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS overall_avg FROM country_avg), above AS (SELECT ca.country, ca.avg_wins FROM country_avg ca, overall o WHERE ca.avg_wins > o.overall_avg), grp AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS group_avg FROM above) SELECT a.country, a.avg_wins, a.avg_wins - o.overall_avg AS above_overall_avg, a.avg_wins - g.group_avg AS above_group_avg FROM above a, overall o, grp g WHERE a.avg_wins > g.group_avg ORDER BY a.avg_wins DESC

d.request: For each circuit country, take the drivers' stored season-to-date win counts from the standings rows at each race held there and average them per race, then average those race figures across the country's races. Which countries are above the average across all countries? Among those, which are also above the average of that above-average group? For each, give the country, its average wins, how far it is above the overall average, and how far it is above the group average.
d.sql: WITH race_avg AS (SELECT r.raceId, c.country, AVG(ds.wins) AS w FROM driverStandings ds JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId JOIN circuits c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country), country_avg AS (SELECT country, AVG(w) AS avg_wins FROM race_avg GROUP BY country), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS o FROM country_avg), above AS (SELECT ca.country, ca.avg_wins FROM country_avg ca, overall ov WHERE ca.avg_wins > ov.o), grp AS (SELECT AVG(avg_wins) AS g FROM above) SELECT a.country, a.avg_wins, a.avg_wins - o.o AS above_overall_avg, a.avg_wins - g.g AS above_group_avg FROM above a, overall o, grp g WHERE a.avg_wins > g.g ORDER BY a.avg_wins DESC
